fika.title: FIKA / A taste of identity
fika.brief: Create a café identity that feels like a small pause with a strong personality. This is a fictional brief created to demonstrate a visual direction.
fika.challenge: Make a familiar coffee moment feel distinctive without relying on the same cups, beans and handwritten clichés.
fika.approach: Start with generous geometric lettering. Give it a flexible rhythm, a confident electric-blue palette and a system that can move from a cup sleeve to a storefront.
fika.results: An adaptable concept identity across packaging, signage and social layouts. No commercial results have been measured.
fika.caption: A LITTLE COFFEE. A DIFFERENT KIND OF ENERGY.
gallery: FIKA identity concept overview with geometric lettering
FIKA brand system and social layout concept

pulse.title: PULSE / Find your rhythm
pulse.brief: Build a social content system for a brand with something clear to say. The fictional campaign explores how a short message can become a recognizable visual beat.
pulse.challenge: Keep a feed connected while giving each post enough freedom to feel fresh.
pulse.approach: Pair oversized type with orbiting lines and deliberate contrast. Repeat the visual rhythm, not the exact same layout, so the content feels like one conversation.
pulse.results: A conceptual content series with room for educational carousels, short statements and campaign announcements. Performance data is not available.
pulse.caption: GIVE YOUR PRESENCE A RHYTHM.
gallery: PULSE campaign poster concept with expressive typography

motion.title: IN MOTION / Every second matters
motion.brief: Imagine a short brand film that turns one geometric shape into a clear story. The displayed artwork is a static art-direction concept, not a finished video.
motion.challenge: Communicate energy and intention quickly, without overwhelming the message with effects.
motion.approach: Use a single triangle, a controlled glow and a sequence of deliberate changes in scale. Build a rhythm that lets the message land before the next movement begins.
motion.results: A concept storyboard and visual language ready to be tested in animation. No finished film or campaign performance is claimed.
motion.caption: IDEAS DON’T STAND STILL.
gallery: IN MOTION sequence and motion-system concept

form.title: FORM / An identity taking shape
form.brief: Create a visual identity for an imagined design studio that believes useful ideas can take many forms.
form.challenge: Build a system with enough structure to be recognizable and enough freedom to keep exploring.
form.approach: Let the triangle become a building block. Combine a restrained grid with bold letterforms, then use scale and negative space to create different expressions from the same ingredients.
form.results: A concept identity system spanning editorial layouts, studio stationery and digital applications. It has not been commissioned by a real client.
form.caption: GIVE YOUR IDEA A SHAPE.
gallery: FORM editorial layout and type detail concept

daily.title: DAILY / A reason to stop
daily.brief: Develop a focused advertising direction for an imagined local business. One useful offer, expressed clearly enough to understand at a glance.
daily.challenge: Make the creative feel immediate without turning the message into noise.
daily.approach: Lead with the audience’s need, reduce the copy to one promise and give the next step a clear place in the layout. Explore variations that can be compared in a real campaign.
daily.results: A set of concept ad variants ready for briefing and controlled testing. No spend, conversions or return figures are available.
daily.caption: NOT JUST ANOTHER POST.

frames.title: FRAME BY FRAME / Details tell stories
frames.brief: Explore a visual direction for short product films that make the small details feel meaningful. The gallery shows static concept posters.
frames.challenge: Show the product’s value through attention and framing rather than a long list of features.
frames.approach: Choose one detail per moment. Use close composition, a restrained palette and a repeatable framing system to connect a series of short stories.
frames.results: A conceptual shot direction and poster series. Real production assets and verified viewing data should replace these examples before launch.
frames.caption: EVERY DETAIL HAS SOMETHING TO SAY.

start.q: What do I need before we start?
start.a: A little context is enough: what your business does, who you want to reach and what you want to change. Share any existing materials and we’ll help turn that into a useful brief.

scope.q: Can I book one service or a connected package?
scope.a: Both. We can focus on one specific need or connect several services around a larger goal. The scope, deliverables and responsibilities are agreed before the work begins.

timeline.q: How long does a project take?
timeline.a: It depends on the scope, the number of deliverables and how quickly feedback is available. We propose a realistic schedule after understanding the brief rather than promising a fixed timeline before we have the details.

existing.q: Can you work with our existing identity?
existing.a: Yes. We first understand what is already working, then develop content or applications that stay true to your guidelines. If the identity itself needs attention, we’ll explain why before suggesting a separate scope.

ads.q: Is advertising spend included in creative fees?
ads.a: Advertising spend and creative or management fees are scoped separately. Before launch, we agree the objective, budget and reporting approach. No result is guaranteed simply by running a campaign.

remote.a: Yes. Clear briefs, planned check-ins and organized feedback make remote collaboration straightforward. We agree the tools and communication rhythm that suit both teams.

brand-before-logo.title: Your brand starts before the logo.
brand-before-logo.excerpt: Before choosing a color or sketching a symbol, decide what people should understand about your business.

body.heading: Start with a useful question.
body.text: What should someone understand after meeting your business for the first time? A logo can help them remember the answer, but it cannot decide the answer for you. Start with the audience, the problem you solve and the reason your approach deserves attention.

body.heading: Choose a clear position.
body.text: Write one simple sentence about who you help and what makes the experience valuable. Avoid a list of every good quality a company could claim. The more focused the position, the easier it becomes to choose the right tone, imagery and visual details.

body.heading: Build a system, not a souvenir.
body.text: A good identity works beyond the presentation page. It should survive a small social icon, a bilingual headline, a product label and a website button. Test the everyday applications early. They reveal whether the idea is flexible or only looks good in one carefully arranged mockup.

body.heading: Give the identity a job.
body.text: The next time you review a design, ask what it helps the audience understand. That question creates a more useful discussion than whether everyone likes the same shade of blue. The best identity is the one that gives your brand a clear and consistent way to show up.

content-with-a-purpose.title: Content is not filler. Give every post a job.
content-with-a-purpose.excerpt: A calendar full of posts is not the same as a content direction. Start with the audience’s question, then decide the format.

body.heading: A post needs a reason to exist.
body.text: Publishing regularly helps a brand stay present, but presence alone is not a strategy. Before adding a post to the calendar, decide what it is there to do: answer a question, explain a benefit, show how something works or make the next step feel easier.

body.heading: Find the audience’s language.
body.text: Look at the questions customers actually ask and the words they use to ask them. Those conversations are often a better starting point than a generic list of awareness days. Build a few useful content pillars around real needs, then give each pillar a recognizable role.

body.heading: Let the message choose the format.
body.text: Some ideas need a single clear sentence. Others need a carousel, a demonstration or a short video. Choosing the format after the message keeps the design from becoming the goal. The visual should make the idea easier to understand, not make the audience work harder.

body.heading: Review more than the numbers.
body.text: Measure the response in relation to the post’s purpose. Saves can suggest practical usefulness; relevant questions can reveal interest; clicks can help evaluate a next step. Numbers need context. Use what you learn to improve the next month, not simply to fill a report.

landing-page-that-connects.title: A landing page should make the next step obvious.
landing-page-that-connects.excerpt: Clarity, confidence and one useful action matter more than adding another section to the page.

body.heading: Continue the conversation.
body.text: A visitor arrives with an expectation, often shaped by an ad, a social post or a recommendation. The first screen should make it clear they are in the right place. Use the same promise and language that brought them there, then explain why it matters.

body.heading: Make one action feel easy.
body.text: A focused page does not ask every visitor to do five different things. Choose the action that makes sense for the offer, such as sending a project brief or booking a call. Label the button with what happens next, and explain any details that might make someone hesitate.

body.heading: Use evidence you can stand behind.
body.text: Show approved work, relevant details and real testimonials where they help someone decide. If an example is conceptual, say so. An honest page with clear limits builds more trust than a collection of impressive numbers without a source.

body.heading: Check the experience on a real phone.
body.text: Read the headline at a narrow width, open the menu with a keyboard and try the form. Make sure the page loads quickly, the text stays readable and the error messages explain how to continue. Useful design is often the result of removing small obstacles.
